section_summary: This section documents economic conditions, stabilization measures, and foreign trade policies in occupied Japan during December 1949. It features extensive memoranda by the Japan Management Association (Keizai Doyukai) criticizing the deflationary impact of the Dodge Line and proposing sweeping modifications to Shoup Mission tax reforms, asset revaluation, and credit policy. Additional State Department and USPOLAD airgrams and memoranda address foreign trade arrangements, private import-export procedures, telecommunications negotiations, Ryukyu exchange rates, and international restitution claims.

subfiles.about: Transmits two memoranda from the Japan Management Association recommending tax cuts, credit expansion, and yen devaluation.
subfiles.from: William W. Diehl, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits two biased Keizai Doyukai papers criticizing Dodge stabilization policies and Shoup tax reforms, noting Japanese government support.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 859: Financial and Economic Recommendations Made by the Japan Management Association

subfiles.about: Analyzes economic distress caused by the Dodge Line and pound devaluation while urging credit expansion and tax relief.
subfiles.summary: This memorandum by Keizai Doyukai analyzes the severe economic difficulties confronting Japanese industry following the British pound devaluation and the implementation of the Dodge Line stabilization program. It argues that drastic credit contraction, the suspension of Reconstruction Finance Bank lending, and underutilization of U.S. Aid Counterpart Funds have resulted in mounting stockpiles, severe monetary stringency, and impending industrial panic. To avert economic collapse, the association urges substantial credit expansion, the release of export stockpiles to domestic markets, lowering of interest rates, and transitional adjustments to the Shoup tax proposals.
subfiles.title: Recent Conditions of Japan's Economy
subfiles.to: General Douglas MacArthur and the Japanese Government

subfiles.about: Submits corporate tax recommendations and requests modifications regarding fixed asset reappraisal, value-added taxes, and depreciable asset taxes.
subfiles.summary: This paper presents Keizai Doyukai's detailed critique of and counter-proposals to the corporation tax reforms recommended by the Shoup Mission. It recommends flexible asset reappraisal procedures with deferred payment schedules for revaluation gains taxes, particularly for public utilities, shipping companies, and small enterprises. The association also strongly urges postponing or simplifying the novel value-added tax and expanded real estate tax, arguing that local governments lack administrative competence and that excessive tax burdens will cripple industry.
subfiles.title: Proposals concerning the Enforcement of Tax Reform Recommended by the Shoup Mission -- In Particular Reference to Corporation Taxes
subfiles.to: Japanese Government and General Headquarters, SCAP

subfiles.about: Reports on Japanese economic developments regarding telecommunications, Chinese trade balances, import regulations, shipping investments, and Ryukyu exchange rates.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: This airgram reviews multiple Japanese economic and commercial developments compiled by the U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo. It covers telegraph negotiations with Chinese Communists, trade balances and railway tie requests involving Nationalist China, preparations for private import trade under MITI and the Foreign Exchange Control Board, and recommendations to reject Rountree Steamship Lines' investment proposal. Additionally, it reports on Danish-Japanese trade discussions, potential Kailan coking coal imports, and exchange rate recommendations for the Ryukyu Islands.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-347: Weekly Economic Notes

subfiles.about: Requests a copy of the recommendations prepared by the SCAP mission to Okinawa regarding exchange rate and pricing procedures.
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Department of State, Washington
subfiles.summary: Requests a copy of the SCAP mission's recommendations concerning Okinawa's exchange rate, wage levels, and pricing procedures.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-239: Recommendations of the SCAP Mission to Okinawa
subfiles.to: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits ESS findings that Japanese non-ferrous metal exports are absent from Europe due to quality issues rather than market-sharing cartels.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports ESS assurances that Japanese non-ferrous metal exports are confined to Asia by quality factors rather than cartel agreements.
subfiles.title: Airgram on Non-Ferrous Metals Market and Alleged Cartel Agreements

subfiles.about: Reports on Japanese government wage bonuses, foreign shipping investment conditions, domestic stockpile reduction, and various bilateral trade negotiations.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports on government wage bonuses, rejection of Rountree's exchange guarantee, stockpile reductions, and trade negotiations with European, Asian, and Middle Eastern partners.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-375: Weekly Economic Notes

subfiles.about: Transmits the November 1949 monthly economic work summary and situational review for Japan, each accompanied by a one-page summary.
subfiles.from: John M. Allison, Office of Northeast Asian Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Transmits monthly economic work summary and situation review for Japan for November 1949, each with an attached one-page summary.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum: Japanese Economic Review and NA Economic Summary for November, 1949
subfiles.to: W. Walton Butterworth, Office of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Reviews State Department and SCAP actions during November 1949 on Japanese peace treaty terms, appropriations, price controls, and property restitution.
subfiles.from: Office of Northeast Asian Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: This report, accompanied by an executive summary, details State Department and SCAP actions during November 1949 relating to the Japanese economy. Key topics include proposed reductions in the fiscal year 1951 GARIOA appropriation, defending the abolition of export floor prices against international dumping allegations, and opposing the revival of restrictive export control associations. It also covers bilateral trade agreement negotiations, liberalization of travel rules for Japanese technicians, and the resolution of complex restitution claims involving looted gold, diamonds, and German assets.
subfiles.title: NA Economic Summary for November, 1949: Japan
subfiles.to: W. Walton Butterworth, Office of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
